decisions.rationale: These are the smallest set of required, null_rate-0.0 columns that plausibly identify one flight-leg row: year has distinct_count 1, month 6, day 31, carrier_code 16, flight_number 2994, and origin_airport_code 3, combining into a composite key for a single scheduled flight leg per day.
duplicate_row_rate is 0.0 across row_count 166158, so no exact-duplicate rows exist in bronze and dedupe_strategy is set to none.

The operator convention calls for a single calendar DATE column instead of three integer parts, but the proposal's action model maps one bronze column to one silver column and cannot merge year, month, and day into a derived field; they remain three separate required INTEGER columns pending a future multi-column derivation.

dep_time, sched_dep_time, arr_time, and sched_arr_time reach max values of 2400.0 with inconsistent digit widths in their samples (e.g. 1.0 vs 2359.0), so they are kept as INTEGER HHMM/HMM codes rather than cast to TIME/TIMESTAMP, which would misparse values like 2400.
dep_time and dep_delay each show null_rate 0.029388 (4883 of 166158 nulls); operator context states a flight that never departed has no departure time, so nulls are retained rather than imputed.
arr_time (null_rate 0.0307), arr_delay (0.032981), and air_time (0.032981) share comparable null rates consistent with flights that never completed, so all three are retained nullable.
tailnum has null_rate 0.009154 (1521 of 166158 nulls); retained nullable since a missing tail number is a plausible data gap, not an error to fail the build on.
_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at, and _airbyte_meta are flagged is_airbyte_metadata true in the profile and carry no business meaning, so all three are dropped.
carrier, origin, and dest are identifier columns per operator context; renamed to carrier_code, origin_airport_code, and destination_airport_code to follow the team's _code suffix convention.

hour (distinct_count 19, null_rate 0.0) and minute (distinct_count 60, null_rate 0.0) are the scheduled departure time already split into parts per operator context; retained as scheduled_departure_hour and scheduled_departure_minute alongside scheduled_departure_time.

purpose: This table provides cleaned, typed NYC flight departure and arrival records for January through June 2013 from EWR, JFK, and LGA, built from the nycflights13 flights source, feeding downstream analytics on carrier performance, delays, and route volumes.
usage: Consumers should treat actual_departure_time, actual_arrival_time, departure_delay_minutes, arrival_delay_minutes, and air_time_minutes as nullable and deliberately filter or account for the roughly 3% of rows where a flight never departed or never completed before aggregating delay metrics; carrier_code, origin_airport_code, and destination_airport_code are short identifiers, not full names. Reconstruct a calendar date by combining year, month, and day until a dedicated DATE column is added in a later revision.
limitations: dedupe_strategy is none because duplicate_row_rate is 0.0 across 166158 rows, so no exact-duplicate removal was required, but this does not guarantee uniqueness on any subset key. The operator's convention of a single calendar DATE column could not be applied because the action model maps one bronze column to one silver column and cannot merge year, month, and day into a single derived field, so they remain three separate INTEGER columns. dep_time, arr_time, dep_delay, arr_delay, and air_time retain nulls (2.9%-3.3% null rates) for flights that never departed or completed, and tailnum retains nulls (0.9%) for unresolved aircraft identifiers; none of these were imputed or dropped.
